questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The most crucial aspects for me when choosing a destination were opportunities to discover new cultures and places, to gain useful knowledge within my fields of study, and to be able to feel comfortable and eventually at home in the city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Due to COVID-19, there have been some restrictions put into place for most of my time here, and these have of course prohibited some social events.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: My home university was very helpful when I needed to gather information. Therefore, it was not a problem to find the information that I needed before my arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus office here has been very helpful in providing the needed information and answering any questions that I might have had. We had an introductory meeting for all the exchange students within my study, which was very informative.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not easy to find housing. I would recommend starting the housing search early and use all available resources and contacts.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is quite expensive to live here in Munich off campus. But it is also my impression that it is nicer to live off campus than on campus. I would recommend, though, to find an apartment or studio with roommates.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are not many on campus housing opportunities for students. There are very limited spots. Therefore, I would not count on getting housing on campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As far as I recall, the registration process was easy and through the host institution's website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Erasmus coordinators and the international office at the host university were happy to help with the registration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for all of the classes that I wanted, and it was easily done at the website.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is possible to follow as many courses as one wants and just sign up for the exams in the courses that one wants to take the exam in. Therefore, I would recommend that students follow more than the required number of classes in the beginning and continue to do so until they are sure of which classes they would like to be examined in.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level here is quite high - comparable to that at the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I would say that the style of teaching is very much the same as that of UCPH. There were lectures held by professors, and we were about 30-60 students in each class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Frontiers in International Trade, Experimental Methods, Economic of Power Markets, The Political Economy of Income Redistribution, and Topics in Applied Econometrics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the courses Frontiers in International Trade, Experimental Methods, and Topics in Applied Econometrics. If students are interested in macroeconomics, performing economic experiments, or applied econometrics, I would recommend these courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I actually had to pay around 150 Euros to study at LMU.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: A gym subscription was less expensive that I had expected. The rent was higher than I expected when I applied to go on exchange in Munich.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
There are not that many non-academic opportunities at LMU. However, there are some sports facilities
near Olympia Parc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was an organisation called MENSA that organised these kinds of activities for Erasmus students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going on as many MENSA activities in the beginning of the semester as one can, because this is a great opportunity for meeting new people and getting to know the area around Munich.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going on trips to nearby cities, go to soccer games, go to Englischer Garten, go a biergarten, or just take a long walk through the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: As the German culture is not that different from the Danish, it was not very difficult.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would recommend joining MENSA activities and look for social groups of exchange students on Facebook.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Germans are rule-followers and very polite.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The politeness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go on as many adventures as possible while here, get a lederhosen/dirndl, and learn to drink beer.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sign up for all the classes you think seem interesting and choose your final courses later on.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experiences that I have gotten with friends, either in Munich or on adventures in nearby cities.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during the exchange has been the restrictions that COVID-19 has put on activities here, especially the social ones.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
